weeks.title: Pier Radio Bench — free-space path loss without marketing
weeks.body_md:
The Pier Radio Bench sits under the Gary pier canopy: a USRP-class SDR, a scratched
ThinkPad, and a laminated card that says COMMERCIAL_STANDARDIZED_6G=false. Week 1 is
ticket WR-4101. Beginners want a 6G slide deck. Operators compute free-space path loss
for a 3.5 GHz pier hop at 120 m using FSPL_dB = 20*log10(d_m) + 20*log10(f_MHz) - 27.55.

Plug numbers on paper before any GUI: d=120, f=3500. That is the only number the lab
accepts. Pasting a vendor '6G ready' banner into the journal fails the claim boundary.

Consensus Ladder for WR-4101: observed = 120 m tape and 3.5 GHz center; inferred = FSPL
dominates this short clear hop; still need = pier-railing multipath (week 6).

Failure mode: claiming 'we have 6G coverage' because a slide said so. Operators speak
`fixtures/wr4101/fspl.json` with d_m, f_mhz, fspl_db. Invented 6G standard IDs fail.

Resource rule: light math fixtures only while Product-Use QEMU is busy — no multi-GB
Sionna/DeepMIMO tarballs on this ticket. Accessibility: journals stay text-first; any
optional plot needs an alt_text field in the portfolio later.

Work the Friis card on paper with a second hop length (95 m at 3500 MHz) so the class
sees how 20*log10(d) moves when the tape changes. Record both answers in the journal
with units. The Pier Radio Bench treats invented '6G coverage radius' strings as claim
boundary failures even when the arithmetic for FSPL is correct.

Operators also name the antenna assumption: isotropic teaching model, not a measured
panel pattern. If someone imports a vendor EIRP table without citing the fixture path
`fixtures/wr4101/fspl.json`, stop the demo and return to the laminated card.

weeks.title: OFDM numerology intuition — symbols without a fake 6G waveform
weeks.body_md:
Ticket WR-4202 ships a toy OFDM numerology card: Δf=30 kHz, N_sc=12 subcarriers per PRB,
symbol duration ≈ 1/Δf ignoring CP. Pier operators compute PRB bandwidth = 12*30e3 = 360 kHz
for scheduling math — not a marketing badge.

One slot with 14 symbols at μ=1 is a teaching fixture, not a claim the pier ships Rel-18.
The lab asks for n_sc, delta_f_hz, prb_bw_hz, and symbol_duration_s. Empty JSON fails.
A print('PASS') string raises AssertionError.

Consensus Ladder: observed = numerology table; inferred = larger Δf shortens symbols;
still need = measured Doppler on the pier.

Failure mode: renaming the week '6G waveform lab' and pasting a vendor constellation
screenshot with no math. Cyclic prefix is a named omission this week — honesty is skill.

Draw one resource block as twelve vertical tones and mark Δf=30 kHz between them.
Compute PRB bandwidth again with μ=0 (15 kHz) as a contrast case: 12*15e3=180 kHz.
Write both results side by side so learners stop treating 'PRB' as a brand badge.

Call out the cyclic-prefix omission in one sentence: CP is real on air interfaces and
deliberately not scored this week. Anyone pasting a constellation PNG without
n_sc/delta_f_hz/prb_bw_hz/symbol_duration_s fields fails the lab contract.

weeks.title: 5G-Advanced features map — Release labels without exam dumps
weeks.body_md:
Ticket WR-4303 is a feature map: RedCap, XR awareness, NTN early hooks, AI/ML study items —
all PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY. List ≥3 Release-18/19 topic labels and one non-claim: this course
does not grant 3GPP membership or dump exam items.

Lab checks features[] length ≥3 with name+release_tag and commercial_6g_exists=false.
If commercial_6g_exists is true, the lab fails.

Consensus Ladder: observed = public overview titles; inferred = 5G-Advanced evolves 5G NR;
still need = measurements mapping to those titles.

NO_AI week: hand-write the map. Generative fill inventing 'Rel-20 commercial 6G' fails the
claim boundary even if grammar is perfect. Alignment file only — no harvested stems.

Build the feature map as three rows only: name, release_tag, PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY.
Example rows may include RedCap, NTN early hooks, and AI/ML study items — never a
fabricated Rel-20 commercial-6G row. commercial_6g_exists stays false in JSON.

NO_AI means hand labels. If a generative draft invents a ratified consumer 6G SKU,
delete the row and rewrite from the alignment file. Membership in 3GPP is not granted
by completing WR-4303.
weeks.worked_example: ≥3 features with release tags; commercial_6g_exists=false.

weeks.title: Link adaptation toy — MCS vs BLER on a fixture
weeks.body_md:
Ticket WR-4404 gives BLER for MCS 0..4 at SNR=8 dB: [0.40,0.22,0.09,0.18,0.35]. Pick the
highest MCS with BLER ≤ 0.1 → MCS 2 at 0.09. Lab checks snr_db, bler_cap, chosen_mcs,

Failure mode: always max MCS for 'throughput.' Empty {} fails. PASS string raises.
Operators speak `fixtures/wr4404/bler_table.json` and defend the choice on a whiteboard.

the maximum eligible index. At SNR=8 dB the eligible set is {2}; chosen_mcs=2 with
bler_at_choice=0.09. Document why MCS 3 and 4 are rejected even if throughput stories
sound better in marketing.

Outer-loop CQI mapping stays in the 'still need' ladder rung — do not claim the pier
runs a live link-adaptation closed loop from this fixture alone.
weeks.worked_example: SNR=8 dB, cap 0.1 → chosen_mcs=2 (BLER 0.09).

weeks.title: NTN LEO delay honesty — light-time, not sci-fi maps
weeks.body_md:
Ticket WR-4505: LEO altitude 550 km, slant ≈700 km. Light-time ≈ d/c; RTT ≈ 2*d/c.
c=3e8, d=7e5 → one_way≈2.333 ms, RTT≈4.667 ms. Not GEO-class (~250 ms). Lab fails if
geo_comparable=true or ntn_as_6g_standard=true.

Consensus Ladder: observed = altitude card; inferred = ms-class RTT for this toy slant;
still need = feeder/gateway scheduling (out of scope).

Marketing fail: 'global 6G NTN' heatmap with no delay math. No constellation sim downloads —
fixture arithmetic only while Stream A runs.

Recompute light-time with a second slant (650 km) so learners practice d/c without
memorizing one number. Compare both RTTs to a GEO-class ~250 ms figure and keep
geo_comparable=false. ntn_as_6g_standard remains false: NTN features in 5G-Advanced
talk are not a commercial standardized 6G ratification.

Refuse constellation-sim downloads while Stream A QEMU is active. Fixture milliseconds
are the graded artifact; heatmaps without delay math are marketing fails.
weeks.worked_example: d=700 km → one_way≈2.333 ms, RTT≈4.667 ms; geo_comparable=false.

weeks.title: Channel tap toy — RMS delay spread on pier railing fixture
weeks.body_md:
Ticket WR-4606: delays_ns=[0,120,350], powers_db=[0,-3,-10]. Compute discrete PDP RMS delay
spread with linear powers. Lab checks tau_rms_ns within tolerance and tap_count=3.

Multipath is a number, not a vibe. Claiming 'AI beamforming solved multipath' without taps
fails. PHYSICAL sounding stays PHYSICAL_PENDING.

Consensus Ladder: observed = tap table; inferred = late energy grows τ_rms; still need =
measured sounding. Empty {} fails. Wrong τ_rms fails. PASS raises.

Convert powers_db to linear, form the first and second moments of delay, then take the
square root for τ_rms. Change the last tap power by −1 dB as a sensitivity check and
note how τ_rms moves. PHYSICAL sounding stays PHYSICAL_PENDING until a real capture
exists; AI beamforming slogans without taps score zero.

Submit delays_ns, powers_db, tau_rms_ns, and tap_count=3. Wrong moments fail even when
the journal prose is polished.
weeks.worked_example: Three-tap PDP → compute tau_rms_ns; tap_count=3.

weeks.title: AI-RAN control loop — gated policy, not magic autonomy

Ticket WR-4707: observe KPI window → propose MCS/PRB action → human gate → apply.
Submit observe_kpis, proposed_action, human_gate=true, auto_apply_without_gate=false.
Ungated auto-apply fails.

AI-RAN is research/systems with gates — not pier-wide 6G autonomy. NO_AI quiz week.
Consensus Ladder: observed = KPI CSV; inferred = actions need gates; still need =
closed-loop field trial evidence (not claimed).

Write the AI-RAN loop as four explicit fields: observe_kpis (list), proposed_action
containing MCS or PRB language, human_gate=true, auto_apply_without_gate=false.
Ungated reinforcement-learning theater fails the validator.

NO_AI quiz week still allows disclosed calculators on the lab JSON. Closed-loop field
trial evidence is not claimed; the pier remains RESEARCH_LAB_SCALE.

On WR-4707, enumerate observe_kpis as concrete CSV column names (bler, prb_util, snr_p50)
before proposing MCS or PRB moves. Document the human gate as a named pier operator role,
not a checkbox theater. Auto-apply without that gate must remain false in every submitted
JSON variant the class practices. Compare one gated proposal against an ungated fantasy
loop and mark which fields the validator rejects. Keep AI-RAN vocabulary at RESEARCH_LAB_SCALE;
do not imply pier-wide closed-loop autonomy from this ticket alone.
weeks.worked_example: human_gate=true; auto_apply_without_gate=false; action names MCS or PRB.

weeks.title: Spectrum honesty — masks and no unauthorized TX

Ticket WR-4808: lab license narrative at 3.5 GHz, OBW 18 MHz. Submit center_ghz, obw_mhz,

Consensus Ladder: observed = license card; inferred = OBW fits mask; still need = real
FCC/ITU filings (not fabricated). NO_AI week. No fake auction wins in journals.

Spectrum honesty is an ethics gate: unauthorized_tx=false, center_ghz=3.5, obw_mhz=18,

SDR' fails the course, not just the week.

Fabricated FCC/ITU PDF filenames are forbidden. Alignment labels are

For WR-4808, recompute whether OBW 18 MHz at 3.5 GHz sits inside the narrative mask and
write mask_ok with the inequality you used. List three transmission acts that would set

courses.title: Robotics and Control — HarborBot Bay
courses.kinesthetic_hook: Ten weeks in HarborBot Bay: frames → 2R kinematics → PID → traj → sensing → E-stop → diff-drive → estimation → message schemas → safety capstone. Real commands on fixture math.
courses.lesson_excerpt:
HarborBot Bay ticket RB-5101: a diff-drive cart on taped pier coordinates. Pose is (x,y,theta)
in meters/radians. Students compute a planar transform of a tool point and refuse 'AI nabbed
the box' stories without a frame diagram.

Lab checks x, y, theta, tool_x, tool_y after a ya
courses.worked_example: theta=π/2, tool offset (0.2,0) → tool maps to pier axes with sin/cos.
courses.assignment: Compute RB-5101 pose/tool map. Submit lab_se2_pose.

syllabus.hook: Control discipline for a civic pier robot cart: transforms, inverse kinematics checks, PID with anti-windup notes, trajectory limits, noise-aware sensing, and hard E-stop policy. ROS topic names are alignment vocabulary only — no claiming a full robot fleet deploy.

weeks.title: HarborBot frames — SE(2) pose without cinematic hype
weeks.body_md:
HarborBot Bay ticket RB-5101: a diff-drive cart on taped pier coordinates. Pose is (x,y,theta)
in meters/radians. Students compute a planar transform of a tool point and refuse 'AI nabbed
the box' stories without a frame diagram.

Lab checks x, y, theta, tool_x, tool_y after a yaw rotation. Empty {} fails. PASS raises.

Consensus Ladder: observed = tape origin and tool offset; inferred = rotation mixes x/y;
still need = wheel slip model (later). Accessibility: ASCII frame diagrams required in journals.

Tape the pier origin, mark +x along the aisle, and sketch the tool offset arrow before
any code. With theta=π/2, show how the offset rotates into pier axes using cos/sin.
Journals without an ASCII frame diagram fail accessibility expectations for HarborBot.

Refuse 'AI nabbed the box' narratives that skip the SE(2) fields. Lab JSON must carry
x, y, theta, tool offsets, and mapped tool_x/tool_y that match the rotation math.
weeks.worked_example: theta=π/2, tool offset (0.2,0) → tool maps to pier axes with sin/cos.

weeks.title: 2R kinematics — reachability before torque myths
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5202: planar 2R arm with L1=0.35 m, L2=0.30 m. Forward kinematics to a target and
a reachability flag when hypot(x,y) > L1+L2. Lab checks x,y, reachable.

Consensus Ladder: observed = link lengths; inferred = workspace is an annulus/disk bound;
still need = joint limits map. Failure: claiming infinite reach because 'servos are strong.'

Plot the reachable disk of radius L1+L2=0.65 m and mark a forbidden point beyond it.
Forward kinematics must report both Cartesian tip and reachable=false when outside.
Strong-servo myths do not enlarge the workspace.

Joint-limit maps stay in 'still need'. Learners defend L1/L2 numbers from the fixture
card, not from a cinematic robot trailer.

For RB-5202, compute tip pose at θ1=0.4 rad, θ2=−0.2 rad with L1=0.35, L2=0.30 and mark
reachable vs hypot(x,y)>0.65. Include a second target beyond the disk and show
reachable=false without inventing extra link length. Defend L1/L2 from the fixture card
only; cinematic reach claims are out of scope. Joint-limit maps stay listed under still-need.
weeks.worked_example: L1=0.35, L2=0.30; point beyond 0.65 m → reachable=false.

weeks.title: PID on a fixture plant — gains with anti-windup note
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5303: discrete PID on e=[1.0,0.6,0.2] with Kp=1.2, Ki=0.4, Kd=0.1, dt=0.1.
Compute u for the last step with simple rectangular integral and backward diff. Include
anti_windup_note length ≥8 when integral magnitude is large.

Consensus Ladder: observed = error series; inferred = D term reacts to slope; still need =
real motor plant ID. Empty fails. Wrong u fails.

Expand the PID step: integrate the error series with rectangular rule, form the
backward difference for D, and compute u on the last sample. When |integral| is large,
anti_windup_note must be a real mitigation sentence (≥8 characters), not an empty string.

Plant identification remains unfinished. Wrong u fails even if the motor 'sounds right'
on a phone video.

Walk RB-5303 with the full e series [1.0,0.6,0.2], accumulate rectangular integral, form
backward Δe/dt, and publish u for the last sample with Kp=1.2, Ki=0.4, Kd=0.1, dt=0.1.
When |integral| grows, anti_windup_note must name a mitigation (clamp, back-calculation)
in ≥8 characters. Wrong u fails even if a phone video of the motor looks smooth.
weeks.worked_example: Compute u_last from fixture gains; document anti-windup note.

weeks.title: Trajectory limits — vmax/amax before cinematic paths
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5404: move 1.2 m with vmax=0.4 m/s and amax=0.5 m/s². Compute minimum time for a
trapezoid/triangle profile bound and reject path_ok if commanded speed exceeds vmax.

NO_AI week. Consensus Ladder: observed = limits card; inferred = time bounded by v/a;
still need = curvature limits. Failure: spline that ignores vmax 'because it looks smooth.'

For distance 1.2 m, vmax=0.4, amax=0.5, derive whether the profile is triangle or
trapezoid, then compute t_min. path_ok is false when cmd_speed exceeds vmax. Smooth
splines that ignore limits fail the NO_AI week.

Curvature limits are deferred. Whiteboard the numbers; screenshots of path planners
without t_min/path_ok fields do not pass.

On RB-5404, decide triangle vs trapezoid for 1.2 m with vmax=0.4 and amax=0.5, then compute
t_min from the chosen profile. Set path_ok false for any cmd_speed>vmax and explain the
reject in one sentence. NO_AI week: hand-derive on paper; GUI path screenshots without
t_min/path_ok fields do not pass. Curvature limits remain deferred.
weeks.worked_example: Distance 1.2 m, vmax 0.4, amax 0.5 → compute t_min; path_ok respects vmax.

weeks.title: Sensor noise — mean/std and reject wild outliers
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5505: lidar range samples [1.01,1.00,0.99,1.02,3.50] m. Compute mean/std after
dropping values beyond 1.5×IQR or a hard gate >2.0 m. Lab checks cleaned_n, mean, outlier_dropped.

Consensus Ladder: observed = samples; inferred = 3.50 is outlier for pier aisle; still need =
calibrated bias. Failure: trusting raw max as truth.

Apply the hard gate (>2.0 m drop) to the lidar list and recompute mean on the cleaned
set. outlier_dropped must be true when 3.50 is removed. Trusting the raw maximum as
aisle truth fails sensing discipline.

Bias calibration remains a later ladder rung. Empty submissions fail student_artifact.

Clean RB-5505 lidar [1.01,1.00,0.99,1.02,3.50] with the >2.0 m hard gate, recompute mean
and cleaned_n, and set outlier_dropped true when 3.50 is removed. Show why trusting the
raw max as aisle truth breaks sensing discipline. Bias calibration stays on the still-need
rung; empty student_artifact still fails.
weeks.worked_example: Drop 3.50; cleaned_n=4; mean≈1.005.

weeks.title: E-stop policy — hard interrupt beats soft hope
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5606: E-stop must assert motors_disabled=true, brake_engaged=true, and
resume_requires_human=true. Software 'slow down' without disable fails.

Consensus Ladder: observed = E-stop wiring card; inferred = safety power path; still need =
SIL certification (not claimed). Ethics: never bypass E-stop for a demo video.

E-stop is hard: motors_disabled, brake_engaged, and resume_requires_human all true.
Soft 'slow down eventually' stories fail. Bypass for demo video is an ethics fail, not
a style choice. SIL certification is not claimed by this course.

Practice the printable large-text E-stop sheet path even when the cart is powered down
for the classroom tabletop.

Assert RB-5606 E-stop fields motors_disabled, brake_engaged, and resume_requires_human
as a triple-true contract. Contrast against a soft 'slow eventually' story that must fail.
Note that demo-video bypass is an ethics fail, and SIL certification is not claimed.
Keep the printable large-text E-stop sheet in the student packet path for tabletop drills.
weeks.worked_example: motors_disabled, brake_engaged, resume_requires_human all true.

weeks.title: Diff-drive ICC — wheel speeds to body twist
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5707: wheel base B=0.40 m, r=0.05 m, wheel rates ω_l, ω_r. Compute v and ω_body.
Lab checks v, omega, and rejects if someone sets B=0.

Consensus Ladder: observed = encoder rates; inferred = ICC geometry; still need = slip
compensation. Wrong kinematics fail even if the cart 'looks right' on video.

Diff-drive: v=(r/2)(ω_l+ω_r), ω=(r/B)(ω_r−ω_l) with B>0. B=0 is rejected before any
division. Video of the cart without v/omega fields is insufficient evidence.

Slip compensation stays in 'still need'. Encoder rates come from the fixture, not from
invented fleet telemetry.

Derive RB-5707 v=(r/2)(ω_l+ω_r) and ω=(r/B)(ω_r−ω_l) with B=0.40, r=0.05 and reject B=0
before division. Publish finite v and omega from fixture encoder rates only. Video without
those fields is insufficient. Slip compensation remains still-need; invented fleet
telemetry is forbidden. Work a second numeric pair (ω_l=2.0, ω_r=2.4) on the whiteboard
and show how ω_body changes sign when the wheel rates swap, still with B>0 enforced.

weeks.title: State estimation toy — fuse odom + range with covariance honesty
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5808: scalar fuse x_odom and x_range with variances. Compute Kalman-ish gain
K = p/(p+r) and x_hat. Lab checks K, x_hat, and refuses cov_zero_lie=true.

Consensus Ladder: observed = two measurements; inferred = lower variance dominates;
still need = full EKF on SE2. Failure: claiming perfect certainty (P=0).

Scalar fuse uses K=p/(p+r) and refuses cov_zero_lie. Walk a numeric example with
p=0.04, r=0.01 and show how lower variance pulls x_hat. Full SE(2) EKF is not claimed
after this toy.

Finite K and two measurements are required; certainty theater fails honesty.

For RB-5808, compute K=p/(p+r) with p=0.04, r=0.01, form x_hat, and refuse cov_zero_lie.
Show how the lower-variance measurement pulls the estimate. State explicitly that full
SE(2) EKF is not earned by this scalar toy. Certainty theater (P=0) fails honesty.
Repeat with p=0.09, r=0.01 and note how K shrinks when prior variance rises, still
refusing any submission that asserts zero covariance as a lie flag.

Plot K versus r for fixed p=0.04 across r in {0.01,0.04,0.16} and write one sentence on why
cov_zero_lie cannot be true for any of those points on RB-5808.
weeks.worked_example: K=p/(p+r); x_hat = x_odom + K*(x_range-x_odom); no zero-cov lie.

weeks.title: Message schemas — /cmd_vel shaped fixtures without fleet claims
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5909: validate a cmd_vel-shaped JSON with linear.x and angular.z finite, and
frame_id='base_link'. Claiming a 50-robot Harbor fleet deploy fails.

NO_AI week. Consensus Ladder: observed = schema card; inferred = units m/s and rad/s;
still need = DDS/ROS distro pin (not claimed as production).

cmd_vel-shaped JSON needs finite linear_x/angular_z and frame_id=base_link.
fleet_claim=false. NaNs fail. NO_AI week: hand-author the schema. Production DDS/ROS
distro pins are not granted by schema vocabulary alone.

Hand-author RB-5909 cmd_vel JSON with finite linear_x, angular_z, and frame_id=base_link.
fleet_claim must be false; NaNs fail. NO_AI week forbids generative schema dumps.
Production DDS/ROS distro pins are not granted by vocabulary alone. Add a negative case
with angular_z=null and show the validator reject text the pier expects learners to cite.

Document a second negative for RB-5909: linear_x set to NaN while angular_z is finite, and show
that fleet_claim must remain false even if a slide deck claims fifty harbor robots. Cite the
schema card fields by name in the journal so the reject is reproducible without a GUI.
weeks.worked_example: linear.x + angular.z finite; frame_id base_link; fleet_claim=false.

weeks.title: Capstone safety packet — E-stop + traj + fuse evidence
weeks.body_md:
Ticket RB-5910: assemble E-stop policy, traj limits, and fuse result digests. Capstone
requires estop_ok=true, labs_passed≥6, and no_device_os_pr=true (do not open device-os PRs).

Career map: robotics technician / controls junior. Accessibility: emergency procedure

Assemble RB-5910 with estop_ok=true, labs_passed≥6, no_device_os_pr=true, and packet_sha256.
Forbid fabricated injury statistics. Keep career mapping as robotics technician / controls
junior — aligned, not granted — and retain the large-text E-stop procedure in portfolio.

weeks.title: Game loop — fixed dt honesty on Forge Arcade
weeks.body_md:
Ticket GA-6101: fixed timestep dt=1/60 with accumulator pattern. Lab checks dt, steps,
spiral_of_death_guard=true when frame_time exceeds 0.25 s clamp. Variable rendering may
interpolate; simulation steps stay fixed.

Consensus Ladder: observed = clock card; inferred = fixed dt stabilizes physics; still need =
profiling on target handheld (PHYSICAL_PENDING). Failure: 'just use delta everywhere' without guard.

Implement the accumulator mental model: fixed dt=1/60, clamp spiral when frame_time
exceeds 0.25 s, keep spiral_of_death_guard true on the reference path. Variable render
interpolation is allowed; simulation steps stay fixed.

Handheld profiling remains PHYSICAL_PENDING. 'Just use delta everywhere' without a
guard fails the loop contract.

On GA-6101, simulate three frame_time samples (0.016, 0.040, 0.30) through the accumulator
with dt=1/60 and show when spiral_of_death_guard clamps. Keep simulation steps fixed while
allowing render interpolation. Handheld profiling stays PHYSICAL_PENDING; delta-everywhere
without a guard fails the loop contract.

weeks.title: AABB collision — overlap math before particle fireworks
weeks.body_md:
Ticket GA-6202: two AABBs. Compute overlap on x and y; hit if both overlap. Lab checks
hit, overlap_x, overlap_y. Failure: particle VFX as 'proof' of collision without math.

Consensus Ladder: observed = rects; inferred = separating-axis for AABB; still need = swept
tests for tunnels. Empty fails.

Compute overlap_x and overlap_y explicitly; hit requires both positive. Particle VFX
cannot replace the arithmetic. Swept tests for tunneling stay in 'still need'.

Submit both rectangles and the overlap fields. Empty {} fails. Wrong signs fail.

Compute GA-6202 overlap_x and overlap_y for two axis-aligned boxes with deliberate miss and
hit cases; require both overlaps positive for hit. Particle VFX cannot replace the signs.
Swept tunneling tests remain still-need. Empty {} and wrong signs fail the lab. Include a
third rectangle pair where overlap_x>0 but overlap_y≤0 and mark hit=false with the arithmetic
written beside the boxes.

weeks.title: Audio clock — beat grid without pirated sample packs
weeks.body_md:
Ticket GA-6303: BPM=120 → beat period 0.5 s. Map t=1.25 s to beat index and phase.
license_ok must be true; pirated_sample_pack=false.

Consensus Ladder: observed = BPM card; inferred = phase in [0,1); still need = device latency
calibration. Failure: cracked sample libraries in the portfolio.

BPM 120 → period 0.5 s. Map t=1.25 to beat_index=2 and phase=0.5. license_ok true and
pirated_sample_pack false are hard gates. Cracked sample libraries in the portfolio
fail the week regardless of beat math.

Device latency calibration remains unfinished; do not invent millisecond offsets.

Map GA-6303 t=1.25 at BPM 120 to beat_index and phase with period 0.5 s. Enforce
license_ok true and pirated_sample_pack false as hard gates. Cracked sample packs fail

courses.kinesthetic_hook: Ten Harbor Desk Voice weeks: consent → conflict → professional tickets → ethics ladder → attribution → feedback → minutes → AI disclosure → a11y → PD capstone. Instructor key material stay out of learner modes.

courses.worked_example: Audience 'Saturday volunteers + walk-up patrons'; purpose 'ticket coaching logs'; classes ticket_id/device_role; retention 90; opt-out via desk lead; ai_disclosure true.

syllabus.hook: Operational ethics and professional communication for public-desk apprentices: consent cards, recusal, ticket tone, observation ladders, citation discipline, feedback rubrics, minutes, AI disclosure modes, and accessible communication. ISC2/CompTIA professionalism names are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY alignment labels — not credentials granted.

weeks.title: Consent on the walk-up desk — name audience and purpose
weeks.body_md:
Harbor Desk Voice opens with a consent card, not a slogan. When a patron asks the desk AI tutor for help on ticket PD-2101, you must say who hears the log, why it is kept, which data classes are stored, how many days it lives, and how to opt out. 'Everyone' is not an audience. 'Improve the product' is not a purpose when the desk's real purpose is coaching a restore path.

Ticket PD-2101 is a walk-up library patron whose essay vanished after idle logout. The tutor may log ticket_id, device_role, and lesson_progress. It must not log SSN, library-card PAN, or passwords. Retention for coaching notes is 90 days unless the desk lead shortens it. Opt-out is spoken: ask the desk lead to disable AI coaching on that ticket.

Consensus Ladder this week: observed = tutor banner missing audience line; inferred = consent incomplete; still need = desk lead confirmation before enabling logging. Fabricating 'ninety percent of patrons consented' is forbidden.

You will write a consent disclosure JSON that names audience, purpose, data_classes (≥2, no ssn), retention_days > 0, opt_out_path, and ai_disclosure=true. Empty {} fails. A file that only says PASS raises. This is professional communication as an operational control, not a poster on the wall.
weeks.worked_example: Audience 'Saturday volunteers + walk-up patrons'; purpose 'ticket coaching logs'; classes ticket_id/device_role; retention 90; opt-out via desk lead; ai_disclosure true.

weeks.title: Conflict of interest — disclose and recuse
weeks.body_md:
Harbor Desk Voice treats conflict as a scheduling problem, not a moral panic. Ticket PD-2204: a Saturday volunteer mentors classmate Jordan on the portfolio while also sitting on the scoring panel for that same portfolio. Mentoring is fine. Scoring after private coaching is not. The fix is disclose_to=course lead and recuse=true when conflict_present=true.

Write the scenario in ≥40 characters with concrete roles. Rationale must explain the unfair advantage without attacking Jordan's identity. 'It's fine' is not a rationale. Recusal without disclosure still fails the desk culture: the lead needs to reassign the scorer.

Consensus Ladder: observed = same person coaches and scores; inferred = grading advantage; still need = alternate scorer name; action = recuse and hand off. Do not invent injury statistics or claim accreditation from a recusal drill.

This week is AI_DISCLOSED for drafting the scenario, but the submitted JSON must be the learner's judgment. Instructor answer keys stay out of learner tutor modes.
weeks.worked_example: conflict_present true → disclose_to course lead + recuse true; rationale names scoring+mentoring overlap.

weeks.title: Professional tickets — no demeaning labels
weeks.body_md:
Professional communication on Harbor Desk Voice is a ticket with a subject ≥8 characters and a body ≥80 characters that names observation and next action. Channel must be email, ticket, or slack_work — not personal SMS for desk work. demeaning_labels must be false. promises_outcome must be false: you do not guarantee the essay will return.

Ticket PD-2307 body that works: idle logout at 1200s discarded unsaved textarea on kiosk 3; check auto-save; coach Save As; no reboot-and-hope. Body that fails: 'you are stupid and lazy' — banned tokens include stupid, lazy, hopeless, idiot.

Consensus Ladder: observed = patron upset; inferred = session loss; still need = auto-save folder existence; action = restore path. Do not promise 'we will always recover every file.'

This is the week learners practice tone as a safety property: demeaning language escalates conflict and contaminates the evidence trail.
weeks.worked_example: channel ticket; subject names kiosk; body ≥80 with restore path; demeaning_labels false; promises_outcome false.

weeks.title: Ethics ladder — observation before inference
weeks.body_md:
The Harbor Desk ethics ladder is observation → inference → need → action, with fabricated_impact forced false. Ticket PD-2409: three patrons report missing USB files after Friday close. Observation names the reports. Inference may say cleanup script. Need asks for cleanup schedule confirmation. Action pauses wipe and posts notice. Claiming 'this harmed 10,000 residents' without measurement is fabricated_impact and fails.

NO_AI week for the ladder write-up: learners must separate what they saw from what they guess without a model filling gaps. AI may be used later to critique structure, but this week's submission is human-authored ladder JSON.

Consensus Ladder is the lab itself. Confusing observation with inference is the most common Harbor Desk failure mode and it poisons meeting minutes next week. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: observation/inference/need/action depth floors; fabricated_impact false; NO_AI for authorship.

weeks.title: Attribution — cite without dumping
weeks.body_md:
Harbor Desk Voice cites PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY sources without harvesting exam stems. Ticket PD-2511 maps ISC2 ethics theme names to conflict drills. quote_chars ≤120. paraphrase ≥40 characters in WAIKE words. reuse_class must be PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY, FAIR_USE_PARAPHRASE, or ORIGINAL. FULL_COPY and 'verbatim dump' fail.

Learners often paste chapter walls into journals. The lab rejects that. Alignment labels are not credentials granted. CompTIA/ISC2 names stay PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY.

Consensus Ladder: observed = source title present; inferred = reuse class chosen; still need = paraphrase quality; action = submit citation JSON. Do not claim the desk grants ISC2 certification. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: reuse_class PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY; quote_chars≤120; paraphrase≥40; no verbatim dump.

weeks.title: Feedback rubric — evidence then score
weeks.body_md:
Feedback on Harbor Desk Voice is criterion → evidence → score 0..4 → next_action, with identity_attack false. Ticket PD-2615 scores a peer journal on observation/inference separation. Evidence must quote the journal behavior, not the person's identity. Score 9 fails. next_action must tell the learner what to try next.

Demeaning feedback is an ethics failure even when the score is numerically correct. 'You always mess up because of who you are' is identity_attack and fails.

Consensus Ladder: observed = journal text; inferred = separation quality; still need = one improvement; action = next_action line. Do not publish grades without human-in-the-loop when acting as educator copilot. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: score 0..4; evidence≥24; identity_attack false; next_action≥16.

weeks.title: Meeting minutes — owners and due dates
weeks.body_md:
Meeting minutes for Harbor Desk Voice require attendees_count ≥2, parallel arrays of decisions/owners/due_dates (≥2 each), and pii_redacted true. Ticket PD-2718 closes the USB wipe decision: Pause USB wipe / desk.lead / 2026-08-18 and Post Friday notice / volunteer.sat / 2026-08-17.

Unequal array lengths fail. Patron names and card numbers must not appear. Minutes are professional communication artifacts that Saturday volunteers can continue without asking you.

Consensus Ladder: observed = decisions spoken; inferred = ownership assigned; still need = due dates; action = publish redacted minutes. Fabricating attendance to look popular fails the ethics bar. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: attendees≥2; parallel decisions/owners/due_dates; pii_redacted true.

weeks.title: AI disclosure modes — keys stay out
weeks.body_md:
AI disclosure modes on Harbor Desk Voice are AI_ALLOWED, AI_RESTRICTED, AI_DISCLOSED, and NO_AI. Ticket PD-2822 requires disclosed=true, learner-key-access=false, learner_facing=true. Learner tutor and mastery benchmark modes must not load the instructor key store. Educator copilot may read keys only with HITL grading — never to whisper finals to learners.

For NO_AI mode, rationale must say human-only or no ai. Silent AI use during NO_AI weeks fails honesty even if the JSON looks fine.

Consensus Ladder: observed = mode banner; inferred = key access forbidden; still need = rationale sentence; action = submit disclosure JSON. This week wires the gunnchAI contract permission split into a lab students can run. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: mode valid; disclosed true; used_key material false; learner_facing true.

weeks.title: Accessible professional communication
weeks.body_md:
Accessibility is part of professional communication, not a sticker. Ticket PD-2925 requires captions=true, plain_language=true, alt_text≥12 characters, color_only_signals=false, and large_print_available=true. Color-only 'red means fail' without text fails. Missing captions on desk explainer videos fails.

NO_AI week for the a11y checklist walkthrough: learners inspect a real flyer mock and mark the five fields honestly. Fabricating disabled-patron quotes is forbidden.

Consensus Ladder: observed = flyer uses red/green only; inferred = color_only_signals true (bad); still need = text labels; action = revise and resubmit. Large-print packets live in the student path. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: captions/plain_language/large_print true; color_only false; alt_text≥12; NO_AI walkthrough.

weeks.title: Capstone — consent, conflict, a11y, no key leak
weeks.body_md:
The Harbor Desk Voice capstone bundles the ethics muscle: labs_passed≥6, consent_ok, conflict_ok, a11y_ok, no_key_leak true, fabricated_impact false. Ticket PD-2A30 is a ship checklist for the professional development portfolio: show empty-fail evidence, claim boundary paragraph, accessibility notes, and career map (aligned not granted).

Career roles: community_desk_coordinator, volunteer_lead, junior_comms_specialist. Certs aligned not granted may list ISC2 ethics themes and CompTIA professionalism domains as labels only.

Consensus Ladder: observed = nine lab JSONs; inferred = ready for portfolio; still need = human playtest of desk scripts (not claimed here); action = submit capstone JSON. REAL_STUDENT_E6 stays false. Cursor never merges. Harbor Desk Voice insists on numbered ticket IDs in journals so a Saturday volunteer can continue without a hallway interrogation. Write the next action as a verb phrase a stranger can execute. Keep patron faces, passwords, and invented harm counts out of the packet. If two tools disagree, write what you saw, then what you guessed, then the missing fact before changing shared systems. Professional development here is measured by reproducible desk artifacts, not by slogans about culture.
weeks.worked_example: labs_passed≥6; consent/conflict/a11y/no_key_leak true; fabricated_impact false.

weeks.title: SQL SELECT with pier filters — honest predicates

weeks.title: MCU memory map — flash vs SRAM before first boot
weeks.body_md: ForgeSense Subsystem Bench ticket EP-4101: MCU memory map — flash vs SRAM before first boot. Map the nRF52840-class memory regions for ForgeSense subsystem firmware. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering, OTA, and carrier claims unless EVT evidence exists. Zephyr/KiCad/gunnchOS docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY — original WAIKE fixture wording only. Empty {} fails. A file whose body is only PASS raises. Show computed JSON fields; GUI screenshots are not acceptance. Distinct from HARDWARE_ENGINEERING SPICE weeks — this course owns firmware/bus/QEMU path. Journal EP-4101: restate the worked numbers, name one claim you refuse (commercial standardized 6G, vendor cert grant, unmerged device-os PR, fabricated field trial), and keep prose specific to this week's lab_id and ticket IDs. On an nRF52840-class part, 1 MB of flash spans 0x00000000-0x000FFFFF and 256 KB of SRAM spans 0x20000000-0x2003FFFF; the first vector-table word is the initial stack pointer and the second is the reset handler address, so a wrong table offset boots into garbage before main() ever runs.
weeks.worked_example: flash_base=0x00000000, sram_base=0x20000000, vector_table_offset=0x100

weeks.title: GPIO contract — direction, pull, and safe defaults
weeks.body_md: ForgeSense Subsystem Bench ticket EP-4202: GPIO contract — direction, pull, and safe defaults. Author GPIO contract JSON before any Zephyr pinmux call. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering, OTA, and carrier claims unless EVT evidence exists. Zephyr/KiCad/gunnchOS docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY — original WAIKE fixture wording only. Empty {} fails. A file whose body is only PASS raises. Show computed JSON fields; GUI screenshots are not acceptance. Distinct from HARDWARE_ENGINEERING SPICE weeks — this course owns firmware/bus/QEMU path. Journal EP-4202: restate the worked numbers, name one claim you refuse (commercial standardized 6G, vendor cert grant, unmerged device-os PR, fabricated field trial), and keep prose specific to this week's lab_id and ticket IDs. Write the inactive output level before switching a pin to output so the line never glitches high at boot; Zephyr's GPIO_OUTPUT_INACTIVE honours active-low wiring, and any input left without a pull resistor floats and reads noise.
weeks.worked_example: pin=LED0, direction=out, default_level=0, pull=none

weeks.title: I2C timing — address, frequency, and NACK recovery
weeks.body_md: ForgeSense Subsystem Bench ticket EP-4303: I2C timing — address, frequency, and NACK recovery. SSD1306-class address 0x3C at 100 kHz with explicit NACK plan. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering, OTA, and carrier claims unless EVT evidence exists. Zephyr/KiCad/gunnchOS docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY — original WAIKE fixture wording only. Empty {} fails. A file whose body is only PASS raises. Show computed JSON fields; GUI screenshots are not acceptance. Distinct from HARDWARE_ENGINEERING SPICE weeks — this course owns firmware/bus/QEMU path. Journal EP-4303: restate the worked numbers, name one claim you refuse (commercial standardized 6G, vendor cert grant, unmerged device-os PR, fabricated field trial), and keep prose specific to this week's lab_id and ticket IDs. A 7-bit address of 0x3C appears on the wire as 0x78 for a write and 0x79 for a read; an address NACK means the device is absent or the address is wrong, and a slave holding SDA low is released by clocking SCL up to nine times and then issuing a STOP.
weeks.worked_example: bus=i2c1, addr=0x3C, freq_khz=100, nack_recovery=true

weeks.title: SPI flash read — opcode and length honesty
weeks.body_md: ForgeSense Subsystem Bench ticket EP-4404: SPI flash read — opcode and length honesty. NO_AI week: hand-author SPI read frame fields. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering, OTA, and carrier claims unless EVT evidence exists. Zephyr/KiCad/gunnchOS docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY — original WAIKE fixture wording only. Empty {} fails. A file whose body is only PASS raises. Show computed JSON fields; GUI screenshots are not acceptance. Distinct from HARDWARE_ENGINEERING SPICE weeks — this course owns firmware/bus/QEMU path. Journal EP-4404: restate the worked numbers, name one claim you refuse (commercial standardized 6G, vendor cert grant, unmerged device-os PR, fabricated field trial), and keep prose specific to this week's lab_id and ticket IDs. Opcode 0x03 is the plain READ command followed by a 24-bit address with no dummy byte; faster clocks need 0x0B FAST READ with one dummy byte, and the CRC must be computed over exactly read_len bytes, not over the buffer allocation.
weeks.worked_example: opcode=0x03, addr=0x00001000, read_len=16, crc_ok=true

weeks.title: ADC scaling — counts to millivolts
weeks.body_md: ForgeSense Subsystem Bench ticket EP-4505: ADC scaling — counts to millivolts. Convert 12-bit ADC count to millivolts with stated vref. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering, OTA, and carrier claims unless EVT evidence exists. Zephyr/KiCad/gunnchOS docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY — original WAIKE fixture wording only. Empty {} fails. A file whose body is only PASS raises. Show computed JSON fields; GUI screenshots are not acceptance. Distinct from HARDWARE_ENGINEERING SPICE weeks — this course owns firmware/bus/QEMU path. Journal EP-4505: restate the worked numbers, name one claim you refuse (commercial standardized 6G, vendor cert grant, unmerged device-os PR, fabricated field trial), and keep prose specific to this week's lab_id and ticket IDs. Millivolts equal raw multiplied by vref divided by 2^bits, so 2048 x 3300 / 4096 = 1650; dividing by 4095 instead gives about 1650.4, so record which convention you used, and remember that SAADC gain and reference settings change the effective full scale.

weeks.title: Sleep modes — wake source honesty
weeks.body_md: ForgeSense Subsystem Bench ticket EP-4909: Sleep modes — wake source honesty. NO_AI week: document wake source without inventing uA draw. PHYSICAL_PENDING covers soldering, OTA, and carrier claims unless EVT evidence exists. Zephyr/KiCad/gunnchOS docs are PUBLIC_REFERENCE_ONLY — original WAIKE fixture wording only. Empty {} fails. weeks.title: Research question and claim ledger
weeks.body_md: Research Bench ticket SGA-1101 opens the apprenticeship with a question small enough to answer: does a codebook prior raise top-3 beam accuracy on a synthetic LEO scenario? Before any code runs, write a claim ledger. Every sentence you might later put in a poster gets one row and one evidence class. SYNTHETIC_SIM means your own simulator produced it, so the claim is only as strong as the model's assumptions. CITED_SPEC means a standards document states it, and the row must name the source_id, for example the 3GPP NTN study TR 38.811. MEASURED means field or bench data exist and the row points at a dataset_ref you can hand to a reviewer. A MEASURED row with no dataset is not a weak claim; it is an open question, and the ledger should say OPEN rather than quietly drop it. The 7GC campuses share one more rule: no row may imply that a university, operator, or vendor endorses the work, so affiliation_claim stays false. Mentors read the ledger before the results, because a tidy chart built on an unlabeled claim is the most common way an apprenticeship poster goes wrong.
weeks.worked_example: claim A: SYNTHETIC_SIM; claim B: CITED_SPEC source_id=3GPP_TR_38_811_NTN; claim C: MEASURED dataset_ref=none-yet status=OPEN

weeks.title: Reproducible runs — config digest, seed, and rerun
weeks.body_md: SGA-1202 turns the week-one question into something another apprentice can rerun on a different campus. A run manifest has four parts. The config text is the exact file the simulator read, byte for byte, and its SHA-256 digest proves which file that was; changing a single newline changes the digest, so the grader recomputes it rather than trusting a pasted hash. The seed must be an integer you chose and wrote down, not the word random, because an unpinned generator makes every comparison later in the course meaningless. The command line is recorded verbatim, including flags, so nobody has to guess which entry point produced a figure. Finally, run the same seed and config twice and report both metrics. If they differ, something nondeterministic is leaking in: thread scheduling, an unseeded library, or a timestamp in the config. Track that down before moving on. Gary, Geelong, and Nubuke cohorts swap manifests in week ten, and a figure whose manifest does not reproduce is removed from the shared packet rather than footnoted.
weeks.worked_example:
config_text='scenario=leo600_sband
seed=20261102
beams=8
epochs=5
' → sha256 recorded; rerun_metric_a == rerun_metric_b == 0.625

weeks.title: NTN propagation delay — nadir one-way and round trip
weeks.body_md: SGA-1303 is the first physics week. A non-terrestrial network puts the base station, or a relay for it, on a satellite, and the first consequence is time. Light covers 299,792.458 km per second, so a low-Earth-orbit satellite directly overhead at 600 km is about 2.0014 ms away one way and 4.0028 ms round trip. A geostationary satellite at 35,786 km is about 119.37 ms one way, which is why GEO links feel sluggish for interactive traffic even with ample bandwidth. These are nadir numbers: the satellite straight above the user. At low elevation the slant range can be several times the altitude, so the real delay is longer, and the lab asks you to state geometry = nadir so nobody mistakes a lower bound for a link budget. The 3GPP NTN study, TR 38.811, discusses why terrestrial timing assumptions such as HARQ round trips and timing advance must be stretched for these distances. The grader recomputes your delay from the altitude you submit, so copying the LEO answer onto a GEO altitude fails, which is exactly the mistake this week is designed to catch.

weeks.title: LEO Doppler — orbital speed and the upper bound
weeks.body_md: SGA-1404 is a NO_AI week: work the numbers by hand and show each line. A satellite in a circular orbit moves at v = sqrt(μ / r), where μ for Earth is 398,600.4418 km³/s² and r is Earth's mean radius of 6,371 km plus the altitude. At 600 km that gives r = 6,971 km and v ≈ 7.5617 km/s, roughly 27,000 km/h. The carrier seen by a ground user shifts by the component of that velocity along the line of sight, so the shift can never exceed (v / c) · f_c. At a 2 GHz S-band carrier the bound is about 50.45 kHz, which is more than three times the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing of a common NR numerology, so uncompensated Doppler would smear subcarriers into each other. The true maximum seen from the ground is somewhat lower because Earth's curvature and the user's own rotation change the geometry, and it falls to zero as the satellite passes overhead. That is why the lab names this an upper bound and sets bound_is_upper = true. A bound is a design margin, not a measurement, and the claim ledger from week one should file it as SYNTHETIC_SIM or CITED_SPEC.

weeks.title: Beam selection — top-1 and top-k accuracy
weeks.body_md: SGA-1505 moves from link physics to the learning problem behind the AI-RAN papers. A millimetre-wave or NTN cell sweeps a codebook of narrow beams, and exhaustive sweeping costs time and overhead. A beam-selection model looks at side information, such as position or a coarse channel estimate, and ranks the beams it thinks are best, so the radio only measures the top few. The honest metric is top-k accuracy: the fraction of samples whose true best beam appears in the model's first k guesses. On the eight-sample fixture in the lab readme, four samples rank the true beam first, giving top-1 = 0.5, and seven of eight contain it within three guesses, giving top-3 = 0.875. Read those numbers together: top-3 tells you a three-beam refinement sweep would usually succeed, while top-1 says the model alone is right only half the time. Top-k also hides how much signal is lost when the second-best beam is chosen, which week nine records as a construct-validity threat. The fixture is synthetic, so dataset_class must say so.
weeks.worked_example: 8 samples; top-1 hits at samples 1,3,5,7 → 0.5; top-3 misses only sample 6 → 0.875

weeks.title: Baseline vs model — paired interval over seeds
weeks.body_md: SGA-1606 asks whether the model actually beats the baseline or merely got a lucky seed. Run both on the same five seeds and subtract run by run; pairing removes the shared difficulty of each seed, which is usually the largest source of spread. The fixture differences are 0.05, 0.02, 0.07, 0.02 and 0.04, with mean 0.04 and sample standard deviation about 0.0212. With only five pairs you need Student's t, not the normal 1.96: t at 0.975 with four degrees of freedom is 2.776, so the half-width is 2.776 × 0.0212 / √5 ≈ 0.0263 and the 95 percent interval runs from about 0.0137 to 0.0663. It excludes zero, so the poster may say the model improved top-3 accuracy on this synthetic scenario, and should print the interval beside the claim. Had the interval crossed zero, the honest sentence would be that five seeds cannot distinguish the two. Notice what the interval does not license: it says nothing about another scenario, a real cell, or a different codebook. That limitation goes into next week's external-validity row, not into a caveat nobody reads.

weeks.title: O-RAN control loops — where an AI model may act
weeks.body_md: SGA-1707 places the week-five model inside a real architecture. O-RAN splits radio control into loops by how fast they must react. Decisions under about 10 ms, such as HARQ retransmission and per-slot scheduling, stay in the distributed unit and its real-time software. Decisions between roughly 10 ms and one second run as xApps on the near-real-time RAN Intelligent Controller, which is where a beam-pair or handover tuning model would live. Anything slower than a second, including training, long-horizon energy policy, and analytics, runs as an rApp on the non-real-time RIC inside service management and orchestration. The non-real-time RIC guides the near-real-time RIC through the A1 interface with declarative policies, while E2 connects the near-real-time RIC to the base-station nodes it controls. The lab gives you three tasks; classify each by its loop latency, cover all three loops, and name the A1 target. Placing model training in the real-time loop is a design error, not an optimisation, and the grader treats it that way. O-RAN Alliance specifications are cited here for topic labels only.
weeks.worked_example: HARQ 1 ms → real_time (DU); handover tuning 100 ms → near_real_time (xApp); energy policy 60 s → non_real_time (rApp); A1 → near_rt_ric

weeks.title: Digital-twin gap — comparison is not calibration
weeks.body_md: SGA-1808 confronts the gap the 7GC papers keep honest. A digital twin predicts received power across a site; the lab's twin gives -95, -97, -99 and -101 dBm at four points, and a separate reference simulator gives -94, -98, -100 and -103 dBm. The errors are -1, 1, 1 and 2 dB, their squares sum to 7, and the root-mean-square error is sqrt(7/4), about 1.32 dB. That number is useful: it says two models of the same site agree to roughly a decibel. It is not calibration. Calibration compares the twin with measurements from the real site, and in this course the count of field samples is zero. With zero measured samples the status must read UNCALIBRATED_NO_MEASUREMENTS and calibrated_claim must be false, however good the agreement looks. Two simulators can share the same wrong assumption, such as an optimistic clutter model, and agree perfectly while both miss reality. Paper I in the research spine records exactly this open gap. The apprentice's job is to state it clearly enough that the next cohort with radio access knows which measurements to collect.
weeks.worked_example: twin − reference = [-1, 1, 1, 2] dB → RMSE = sqrt(7/4) = 1.3229 dB; measured_samples=0 → UNCALIBRATED_NO_MEASUREMENTS

weeks.title: Threats to validity and research ethics
weeks.body_md: SGA-1909 is the second NO_AI week, because the point is your own judgement about your own work. Sort what could make the results wrong into four kinds. Internal validity asks whether the comparison itself is fair: five seeds, a tuned model against an untuned baseline, or a data leak between training and test positions. External validity asks whether the result travels: one synthetic LEO scenario says little about a dense Gary street canyon or a Geelong port. Construct validity asks whether the metric measures what you care about: top-k accuracy ignores how many decibels are lost when the second-best beam is used. Conclusion validity asks whether the statistics support the sentence: five paired runs give a wide interval, and testing many metrics invites a lucky one. Then restate the guardrails every 7GC research program shares. Use synthetic data only. Never use private competition IQ captures, even if a teammate offers them. Make no claim that a university, operator, or agency endorses the work. A reviewer who sees honest threats listed early trusts the remaining claims more, not less.
weeks.worked_example: internal: 5 seeds; external: one synthetic scenario; construct: top-k ignores SNR loss; conclusion: n=5, wide CI

weeks.title: Research capstone — traced figures, no submission claim
weeks.body_md: SGA-1A10 assembles the packet that cohorts on different campuses exchange. It contains the week-one claim ledger, updated with what the term actually showed, and at least one figure. Every figure carries the config digest and seed from its manifest, so a reader in Nubuke can regenerate the Gary figure without emailing anyone. The packet names its evidence class, which for this course is SYNTHETIC_SIM end to end, and repeats the week-eight gap in plain words. It also states what it is not: submitted_claim stays false, because drafting a figure for the research spine is not the same as submitting a paper, and only the program owner decides when a manuscript goes out. Mentors review the packet against six or more passed labs, check that no instructor answer key leaked into the learner folder, and rerun one figure from its manifest in front of the apprentice. A packet that survives that rerun is a real research artifact at apprentice scale. It is not a publication, a credential, or evidence of deployment, and the closing slide says so.
weeks.worked_example: labs_passed=9; figure topk_vs_codebook carries config_sha256 and seed 20261102; submitted_claim=false; evidence_class=SYNTHETIC_SIM

syllabus.hook: CYBER_SOC COURSE_DIGITAL_RC: analyst-desk numeracy for a junior SOC seat — log parsing, windowed detection, precision and recall, indicator hygiene, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, email authentication, CVSS v3.1, triage queues, and shift metrics. Defensive only, synthetic logs, documentation IP ranges. Distinct from the CYBERSECURITY Harbor SOC governance course. Not student/teacher E6.

weeks.title: Auth log anatomy — failures, sources, and the success that follows
weeks.body_md: Ticket SOC-2101 lands at 01:20 on the Night Shift Desk: eight lines from the bastion host's sshd log and a request to say whether anything matters. Read a log line left to right as a sentence. The timestamp says when, the host and process say where, and the message says what happened to whom from which address. In this fixture 203.0.113.45 fails three times as root, 198.51.100.7 tries the made-up accounts admin and oracle twice, and 192.0.2.10 fails once right after the user naiya logged in with her key from the same machine. Counting failures per source is the start, not the finding. The line that changes the night is the last one: Accepted password for root from 203.0.113.45, seconds after that address failed. A success that follows a run of failures from the same source is the pattern analysts escalate, because it can mean a guessed password. Naiya's typo after a good key login is noise you note and move past. All addresses here come from documentation ranges, so nobody's real server appears in the course, and you never paste a live customer log into a chat tool to save time.
weeks.worked_example: 203.0.113.45 failed 3×, 198.51.100.7 failed 2×, 192.0.2.10 failed 1×; Accepted password for root from 203.0.113.45 at 01:15:31 → escalate

weeks.title: Windowed detection — a threshold means nothing without a clock
weeks.body_md: SOC-2202 asks you to turn last night's eyeballing into a rule the SIEM can run. 'Four failed logins' is not a rule until you say within how long. The fixture lists eleven failures with second offsets. With a threshold of four inside a sixty-second sliding window, 203.0.113.45 fires at second 70: the failures at 20, 50, 65 and 70 all sit within sixty seconds of each other, while the first one at second 0 has already aged out. 198.51.100.7 never fires, because its attempts at 200, 230, 250 and 265 span sixty-five seconds, one heartbeat too slow. Widen the window to ninety seconds and that address alerts at 265 as well. Neither choice is free. A wider window catches slow guessing and also pulls in people who mistype their passwords on a cold morning. Write the threshold and window into the rule's description so the next analyst can reason about a miss, and replay the rule against stored events before you switch it on. The lab grader replays your parameters, so it rejects an alert list that would only be true for a different window.
weeks.worked_example: threshold 4 in 60 s → 203.0.113.45 fires at t=70 (events 20, 50, 65, 70); 198.51.100.7 does not; widen to 90 s → it fires at 265

weeks.title: Detection quality — precision, recall, and the analyst's hour
weeks.body_md: SOC-2303 is a NO_AI week: do the fractions on paper and show each line, because these four numbers decide whether a rule stays on. A month of the brute-force rule produced 60 alerts. Eighteen were real attacks, true positives, and forty-two were not, false positives. Six real attacks slipped through without an alert, false negatives, and 934 quiet events were correctly left alone. Precision asks how often an alert is worth opening: 18 out of 60, or 0.30. Recall asks how many real attacks the rule caught: 18 out of 24, or 0.75. The false-positive rate compares wrong alerts with all benign events, 42 out of 976, about 0.043, which sounds tiny and still costs forty-two investigations. At ten minutes each that is seven analyst-hours spent proving nothing happened. A precision under one half means most alerts are noise, so the honest call is needs tuning, not 'the rule works'. Tuning that raises precision often lowers recall, so record both before and after a change, and never report recall alone because it flatters a noisy rule.
weeks.worked_example: TP 18, FP 42, FN 6, TN 934 → precision 18/60 = 0.30, recall 18/24 = 0.75, FPR 42/976 = 0.043 → needs tuning

weeks.title: Indicator hygiene — hash it, defang it, then compare
weeks.body_md: SOC-2404 arrives with a suspicious attachment name and a link from a user report. Indicators of compromise are only useful if you can compare them exactly and pass them around safely. For files that means a cryptographic hash: SHA-256 turns any sequence of bytes into a 64-character fingerprint, and a single changed byte produces an unrelated digest, so the lab recomputes the hash from the inert sample text instead of trusting a pasted value. For links it means defanging before the indicator goes into a ticket, chat, or report: write hxxp instead of http and bracket every dot in the host, so update-check.example.net becomes update-check[.]example[.]net and nobody's mail client turns it into a clickable trap. Only after both steps do you check the desk's indicator list. Here the sample hash and the domain are both on it, so the answer is a match and the ticket goes to the phishing playbook. A miss does not mean safe, it means unknown, and the course's sample is inert text, never real malware, so nobody downloads or detonates anything on a personal laptop.
weeks.worked_example: sha256('WAIKE-SOC training sample: …') = fc6c0f88…e657; http://update-check.example.net/payload → hxxp://update-check[.]example[.]net/payload; on IOC list → match

weeks.title: ATT&CK mapping — describe behaviour, not villains
weeks.body_md: SOC-2505 gives the desk five behaviours seen this week and asks for a shared vocabulary. MITRE ATT&CK is a public catalogue of attacker techniques, each with an ID and one or more tactics that say what the attacker was trying to achieve. Many failed SSH logins from one address are T1110, Brute Force, under credential access. A never-before-seen account logging in at three in the morning with a correct password is T1078, Valid Accounts, which ATT&CK lists under several tactics because stolen credentials help an intruder get in, stay in, and blend in. A spoofed invoice attachment is T1566, Phishing, under initial access. PowerShell launched with an encoded command line is T1059, Command and Scripting Interpreter, under execution, and files renamed with a .locked suffix beside a ransom note are T1486, Data Encrypted for Impact. Mapping lets the day shift, the detection engineers, and management talk about the same thing. It does not tell you who did it. Plenty of groups use the same techniques, so the lab requires actor_attribution_claim to stay false.
weeks.worked_example: B1 brute force → T1110 credential_access; B3 spoofed invoice → T1566 initial_access; B5 .locked files → T1486 impact; actor_attribution_claim false

weeks.title: Email authentication — passing is not the same as aligned
weeks.body_md: SOC-2606 compares two invoices that both claim to come from Harbor Pay. SPF checks whether the sending server is allowed to send for the envelope's return-path domain. DKIM checks a signature made with a key published by the domain in the signature's d= tag. Both can pass for a domain that has nothing to do with the address the reader sees in the From line. DMARC closes that gap with alignment: at least one passing check must belong to the same organisational domain as the visible From address. Under relaxed alignment, subdomains count, so in message A the From address mail.harborpay.example, the return path bounce.harborpay.example, and the DKIM domain harborpay.example all share harborpay.example, and DMARC passes. Message B also shows SPF pass and DKIM pass, but both checks vouch for bulk-sender.example while the From line says harborpay.example, so DMARC fails. That is exactly the shape of a convincing spoof, and a user who sees 'SPF pass' in a header viewer will be fooled unless someone on the desk explains alignment.
weeks.worked_example: A: From mail.harborpay.example, SPF via bounce.harborpay.example, DKIM d=harborpay.example → aligned → DMARC pass; B: From harborpay.example, SPF/DKIM pass for bulk-sender.example → not aligned → DMARC fail

weeks.title: CVSS v3.1 by hand — from vector string to severity band
weeks.body_md: SOC-2707 is the second NO_AI week, because a desk that only reads scores off a website cannot defend them in a patch meeting. The FIRST CVSS v3.1 base score turns eight metrics into a number. Impact starts from the confidentiality, integrity, and availability weights, 0.56 for High, 0.22 for Low, 0 for None, combined as ISS = 1 − (1 − C)(1 − I)(1 − A). For an unchanged scope, impact is 6.42 × ISS. Exploitability is 8.22 × attack vector × attack complexity × privileges required × user interaction, where a network vector weighs 0.85 and low complexity 0.77. For the familiar AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H vector, ISS is about 0.9148, impact about 5.873, exploitability about 3.887, and their sum rounds up to 9.8, Critical. Roundup means the next tenth upward, not the nearest, which is where hand scorers slip. A local, low-privilege flaw that only leaks data, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N, lands at 5.5, Medium. The base score describes the flaw, not your network; asset value enters next week.
weeks.worked_example: AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H → ISS 0.9148, impact 5.873, exploitability 3.887 → Roundup 9.8 Critical; AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N → 5.5 Medium

weeks.title: Triage queue — severity meets asset criticality
weeks.body_md: SOC-2808 hands you six open alerts at once and one pair of hands. Severity alone is a poor sort key, because a critical alert on a lobby kiosk can matter less than a high alert on the domain controller. The desk multiplies a severity weight, four for critical down to one for low, by the asset's criticality from one to three. A5, critical on a criticality-three server, scores twelve and goes first. A1, high on criticality three, scores nine. A3 and A6 both score six, so the earlier arrival, A3 at minute two, goes ahead of A6 at minute eight. A2, the critical alert on a criticality-one kiosk, scores four, and A4 scores three. Each alert also gets a due time: the minute it arrived plus the service-level target for its severity, fifteen minutes for critical, an hour for high, four hours for medium, a day for low. That puts A2's due time at minute 27 even though it sits fifth in the queue, which is a signal to ask for help rather than quietly breach the target. A queue is a plan you can explain to the shift lead, not a mood.
weeks.worked_example: priority = severity weight × criticality: A5 12, A1 9, A3 6 (t=2), A6 6 (t=8), A2 4, A4 3; due = received + SLA (critical 15, high 60, medium 240, low 1440)

weeks.title: Shift metrics — MTTD, MTTR, and the median that resists one bad night
weeks.body_md: SOC-2909 asks how the week went, in numbers management will read. Mean time to detect is the average gap between when something happened and when the desk noticed. The four incidents took 12, 45, 5 and 70 minutes to detect, so MTTD is 33 minutes. Mean time to resolve, measured here from detection to resolution, averages 78, 65, 35 and 150 minutes to 82. Define the start and end points in the report, because some teams measure resolution from occurrence and their numbers are not comparable with yours. One slow detection, the seventy-minute ransomware case, pulls the mean up; the median of the four detection times is 28.5 minutes and tells a steadier story about a typical night. Report both, and name the outlier instead of hiding it, since that is the incident the next tuning effort should study. Four incidents are a tiny sample. A dashboard that celebrates a five-minute drop in MTTD between two such weeks is reporting noise, so the course asks for the numbers and a sentence about how much they can bear.
weeks.worked_example: time to detect = 12, 45, 5, 70 min → MTTD 33, median 28.5; time to resolve from detection = 78, 65, 35, 150 → MTTR 82

weeks.title: Shift handoff — open incidents, NIST phases, and clean boundaries
weeks.body_md: SOC-2A10 closes the night. A handoff is the document the day shift reads with its first coffee, so it must be complete without you in the room. List every open incident with its ATT&CK technique ID, the NIST SP 800-61 phase it is in, and a named next owner. The phases are preparation, detection and analysis, containment with eradication and recovery, and post-incident activity; saying 'containment' tells the reader which actions are already done and which are waiting. Carry the shift's MTTD and MTTR from last week's calculation rather than rounding them in your head, and say what changed in the rules you tuned. Two boundaries close every Night Shift Desk packet. It contains no real customer data, only the course's synthetic logs and documentation addresses, and it contains no offensive tooling: the desk detects, contains, and documents; it does not build exploits or scan systems it does not own. Mentors check the packet against six or more passed labs and ask you to walk one incident from first log line to current phase out loud.
weeks.worked_example: I4 open: T1486, containment_eradication_recovery, next owner day-shift lead; MTTD 33, MTTR 82; real_customer_data false; offensive_tooling false
